question: What is the suffix for -OH group according to IUPAC?
solution:
Correct Answer **-ols**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__Explanation__:

__
 
• The presence of the -OH group in an inorganic compound may lead to the formation of a BASE.
 
• Say, for example, sodium, which is an inorganic element. When the hydroxy group is combined with sodium, it forms sodium hydroxide which is basic in nature.
 
• The confirmation is obtained through the Arrhenius concept, which states that the compounds that contain hydroxyl (OH-)ions and emit OH- ions by ionization is called a base and on dissociation, NaOH releases a significant amount of OH- ions. As a result, it is called a base.
 
• Other examples are Calcium and zinc.
 
• Both are inorganic compounds and when a hydroxy group, that is, -OH is attached with them, they form a base. 

Hence the correct answer is that the presence of the -OH group in an inorganic compound leads to the formation of a base.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__Concept:__

IUPAC nomenclature:

__
 
• A systematic method of naming organic compounds.
 
• Naming is based on their structures.
 
• It is devised by the International Union of Pure and Applied chemistry.
 
• Many rules are followed while naming the compounds and it is different for different functional groups.
 
• The rules are known as IUPAC rules.
